clues: This is the capital and largest city of Niger, in the west of the country. It sits on the left bank of the Niger River.
This is one of the hottest big cities in the world. It can face long dry spells and floods, and its river is its only water source.
Long ago, local groups lived in small villages here. In 1901, a French captain set up a small army post at this spot.
In the 1970s and 1980s, a boom in mining for uranium made the city grow fast. Dry spells in the farms also pushed many folks to move here.
A bridge named Kennedy links the main city to the far bank of the river. It was built in the years after the land won its freedom in 1960.
